Shumsk Old Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Ternopilska oblast, Ukraine

Demolished. Shumsk's Jewish community, present from the first half of the 18th century, built a beit-midrash, bath, and rental stores in 1745, and its Great Synagogue in 1781; the population reached an extraordinary 1,962 people (86.8 percent of the town) by 1897, supporting five synagogues, most of them followers of Olyka or Trisk Hasidism. On July 10, 1941, the day of the German occupation, Ukrainians began a pogrom; the ghetto's liquidation saw 1,792 people executed on August 18, 1942, and the last remaining Jews murdered that September. Only 15 Jews of Shumsk survived the war. This, the older of Shumsk's two Jewish cemeteries, was demolished in 1959.
